data.name: Nawwaar
data.gender_notes: Nawwaar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘an-Nawwār’, meaning 'the guiding lights'. This name holds a significant place in Islamic history as it was the title given to Prophet Moses’ (as) brother, Harun (Aaron). He was entrusted by Allah to lead the Children of Israel during Prophet Moses’ (as) absence, and thus, became a beacon of guidance for his people.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of guidance and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Nawwaar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guiding Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nawwaar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nawwaar is rooted in Islamic history and has been passed down through generations. It carries a rich cultural significance as it has been associated with leaders and guides. In Islamic literature, the character Harun (Aaron), Prophet Moses’ brother, is known as Nawwaar. He is a historical figure who was chosen by Allah to lead the Children of Israel in Prophet Moses’s absence. During Harun’s (Nawwaar) leadership, the Israelites found direction and stability. The name remains a source of inspiration, urging individuals to become beacons of guidance and light in their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Nawwaar embodies the essence of being a light and a guide for others. It reminds us of the importance of leadership and the role we play in guiding and influencing those around us. As believers, it is expected of us to illuminate the path for those in our circle of influence, and to provide spiritual guidance in times of uncertainty. By adopting the name Nawwaar, one acknowledges their responsibility to be a source of light and a beacon of guidance not just in real-life circumstances, but also spiritual ones, actively working towards providing solace to others and helping them on their journey towards self-improvement and enlightenment.
